newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish EMU support edges up, opponents keep lead.
newsitem.headline: Finnish EMU support edges up, opponents keep lead.

text.p: Domestic support for Finnish membership of Europe's single currency (EMU) has increased slightly from a year ago but opponents still outnumber those in favour, according to a poll published at the weekend.
The survey was conducted by polling institute Taloustutkimus Oy on behalf of Eurooppalainen Suomi, a pro-EU association.
It said in a statement 38 percent supported and 41 percent opposed EMU in the survey of 1,993 people carried out between January 7 and February 5, 1997.
In a similar poll in November-December 1995, 45 percent opposed EMU while 36 percent supported Finnish participation in the single currency.
About one fifth were undecided in both polls.
Men, people in southern Finland, young people, and people in higher positions in the labour market and other white-collar employees were generally more pro-EMU, the association said.
Women, people in northern and other rural areas, older people, farmers and blue-collar workers were against membership, it said. --Helsinki Newsroom +358 - 9 - 680 50 245
